citations.B1: Check-then-act race: `get` then `counts[user_id] = count + 1` lets two threads read the same count and both write
citations.B2: Lost updates on the increment itself: `count + 1` is not atomic across the read/write pair — do the increment inside the same critical section as the read.
citations.B3: replace with an atomic increment under a lock, or `dict.setdefault` plus a per-user lock
citations.B4: No time window: counts never reset, so the limiter permanently blocks a user after 100 lifetime requests
citations.B5: Unbounded memory growth: every distinct `user_id` leaks an entry forever
citations.B6: In-process state only: a dict guards one process, so N workers permit N×limit
citations.B7: No validation of `user_id`: `None`, `""`, or an unhashable value either silently share a bucket or raise `TypeError`
